steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Receipt extraction is a task that has broad implications for automating business processes, improving financial analysis, and making inventory management efficient. By capturing and extracting information from scanned receipts, organizations can streamline their operations, get valuable insights, and make informed decisions. Take restaurant receipts as an example. From them one can extract details like the dates of the transactions, the list of ordered items (with their names and prices), and more. Being able to extract this information accurately is crucial for businesses in several ways: it enables Expense Tracking, it facilitates Financial Analysis, and it helps with the Automation of Business Processes. Figure 1 shows an example of a key information extraction task, which involves recognizing and extracting the information from the item name. Being able to extract this information accurately is crucial for businesses to track expenses, analyze consumer preferences, and manage inventory effectively.

How effective receipt extraction systems are depends crucially on whether there are high-quality datasets that mirror the complexities of real-world receipts. But creating such datasets is challenging because receipts are diverse, and they can vary a lot in layout, language, and information density.

In this paper we present a novel and extensive dataset for the task of receipt extraction, which we call AMuRD (Annotated Multilingual Receipt Dataset). We built this dataset with two main objectives, key information extraction and item classification from scanned receipts. Existing datasets have contributed a lot to the field, but there is still a pressing need for multilingual datasets that cover diverse linguistic and contextual nuances. Our dataset addresses this gap with a collection of receipts in both Arabic and English, and it is a versatile resource for advancing information extraction techniques.

- Contents
  - 47,720 samples; retail stores, restaurants, supermarkets
  - human annotations: item names, classes, weight, number of units, total price, packaging details, units, brand names
  - 37,419 unique item names; 44 product categories
  - weight, number of units, size of units, price, total price
  - packaging info + presence indicators -> consumer behavior, pricing trends, promotional strategies
- Multilingual challenges (Arabic, English): complexity and variability; later sections discuss impact on accuracy and efficiency
- Contributions
  - (1) AMuRD, multilingual (Arabic + English), 47,720 samples from many sources
  - (2) key information extraction + item classification; field annotations; 44 categories
  - (3) tested several language model architectures; fine-tuned LLama; F1 0.76, accuracy 0.68

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Receipt extraction is a task that has broad implications for automating business processes, improving financial analysis, and making inventory management efficient. By capturing and extracting information from scanned receipts, organizations can streamline their operations, get valuable insights, and make informed decisions. Take restaurant receipts as an example. From them one can extract details like the dates of the transactions, the list of ordered items (with their names and prices), and more. Being able to extract this information accurately is crucial for businesses in several ways: it enables Expense Tracking, it facilitates Financial Analysis, and it helps with the Automation of Business Processes. Figure 1 shows an example of a key information extraction task, which involves recognizing and extracting the information from the item name. Being able to extract this information accurately is crucial for businesses to track expenses, analyze consumer preferences, and manage inventory effectively.

How effective receipt extraction systems are depends crucially on whether there are high-quality datasets that mirror the complexities of real-world receipts. But creating such datasets is challenging because receipts are diverse, and they can vary a lot in layout, language, and information density.

In this paper we present a novel and extensive dataset for the task of receipt extraction, which we call AMuRD (Annotated Multilingual Receipt Dataset). We built this dataset with two main objectives, key information extraction and item classification from scanned receipts. Existing datasets have contributed a lot to the field, but there is still a pressing need for multilingual datasets that cover diverse linguistic and contextual nuances. Our dataset addresses this gap with a collection of receipts in both Arabic and English, and it is a versatile resource for advancing information extraction techniques.

AMuRD has 47,720 samples from a wide range of sources, including retail stores, restaurants, and supermarkets. Human annotations are provided for various receipt fields to allow granular analysis and information extraction. The annotations include item names, classes, weight, number of units, total price, packaging details, units, and brand names. The dataset has 37,419 unique item names and allows classification into 44 distinct product categories, which helps organize the items. It also gives detailed information on weight, number of units, size of units, price, and total price, which gives insights into quantitative aspects of the purchased items. Because packaging information and presence indicators are captured, researchers can study consumer behavior, pricing trends, and promotional strategies within receipts.

Receipt extraction in multilingual settings such as Arabic and English brings unique challenges that come from the inherent complexity and variability of these documents. In the following sections we look at some of these key challenges and discuss how they affect the accuracy and efficiency of information extraction systems in this domain.

To sum up, our contributions in this paper are:

- (1) We introduce AMuRD, a novel multilingual dataset for receipt extraction. It has both Arabic and English content, which addresses the pressing need for datasets for diverse linguistic contexts. The AMuRD dataset is extensive, with 47,720 samples from a wide range of sources, so it is rich and practically relevant.

- (2) Our dataset focuses on two challenges in receipt understanding, key information extraction and item classification. It has annotations for various receipt fields, which allows understanding each item on the receipt. It also allows classification into 44 distinct product categories, which helps organize the items.

- (3) We tested several language model architectures and we also fine-tuned a specific model, which we call LLama. We tested this fine-tuned LLama model on AMuRD, and it achieved an F1 score of 0.76 and an accuracy of 0.68. These results show that our approach is effective in extracting key information and classifying items accurately.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Receipt extraction [1,2,3,4,5,6] is a task with broad implications for automating business processes, enhancing financial analysis, and enabling efficient inventory management. By capturing and extracting information from scanned receipts, organizations can streamline operations, gain valuable insights, and make informed decisions. Consider the example of restaurant receipts, from which one can extract details such as the dates of the transactions, the list of ordered items (including their names and prices), and more. The ability to accurately extract such information is crucial for businesses in several ways: it enables Expense Tracking, facilitates Financial Analysis, and aids in the Automation of Business Processes. Figure 1 shows an example of a key information extraction task that involves recognizing and extracting the information from the item name. Accurately extracting such information is crucial for businesses to track expenses, analyze consumer preferences, and manage inventory effectively.

The effectiveness of receipt extraction systems depends crucially on the availability of high-quality datasets that mirror the complexities of real-world receipts. However, creating such datasets is challenging due to the diverse nature of receipts, which can vary greatly in layout, language, and information density.

In this paper, we present a novel and extensive dataset, called AMuRD (Annotated Multilingual Receipt Dataset), tailored to the task of receipt extraction. The dataset was constructed with two primary objectives: key information extraction and item classification from scanned receipts. While existing datasets have contributed significantly to the field, the need for multilingual datasets that encompass diverse linguistic and contextual nuances remains pressing. Our dataset addresses this gap by providing receipts in both Arabic and English, offering a versatile resource for advancing information extraction techniques.

AMuRD encompasses 47,720 samples from a wide array of sources, including retail stores, restaurants, and supermarkets. To facilitate granular analysis and information extraction, human annotations are provided for various receipt fields, including item names, classes, weight, number of units, total price, packaging details, units, and brand names. Our dataset includes 37,419 unique item names and enables classification into 44 distinct product categories, enhancing the organization of items. It further provides detailed information on weight, number of units, size of units, price, and total price, offering insights into the quantitative aspects of purchased items. By capturing packaging information and presence indicators, researchers can study consumer behavior, pricing trends, and promotional strategies within receipts.

Receipt extraction in multilingual settings, such as Arabic and English, introduces unique challenges stemming from the inherent complexity and variability of such documents. In the subsequent sections, we explore some of these key challenges and discuss their implications for the accuracy and efficiency of information extraction systems in this domain.

To sum up, our contributions in this paper are as follows:

- (1) We introduce AMuRD, a novel multilingual dataset tailored for receipt extraction. It encompasses both Arabic and English content, addressing the pressing need for datasets that cater to diverse linguistic contexts. The AMuRD dataset is extensive, comprising 47,720 samples from a wide array of sources, ensuring its richness and practical relevance.

- (2) Our dataset focuses on two challenges in receipt understanding: key information extraction and item classification. It includes annotations for various receipt fields, enabling an understanding of each item on the receipt, and it enables classification into 44 distinct product categories, enhancing the organization of items.

- (3) We tested several language model architectures and fine-tuned a specific model, which we refer to as LLama. Tested on AMuRD, this fine-tuned LLama model achieves an F1 score of 0.76 and an accuracy of 0.68. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in extracting key information and classifying items accurately.
